statuses.implemented: The code is in the repository and its tests pass in CI. It has run only on recorded or synthetic inputs, or has no recorded end-to-end run.
statuses.integrated: Wired into the path a user takes (a command, a workflow or the site) and exercised there by a CI job or a recorded run. No published result rests on it.
statuses.measured: A recorded CI run produced a result that the README, the site or a bench record publishes. The row links the run.
statuses.experimental: Built and possibly run, but parked, a trial, or advisory and unmeasured. Do not rely on it; it may change or go.

grades.fixture: Saved or synthetic data, for demos and tests. Never clears a release.
grades.diagnostic: A real run: the engine or the browser ran, or a live model answered, on a developer's machine or a CI runner, with isolation as declared. Does not clear a release.
grades.isolated: The game ran sandboxed with no network, the checks came from the base commit, and a separate trusted job judged and signed. No row has this grade yet: the replay sandbox (#253), the two-job action (#254) and the receipt (#255) are open.
grades.protected: Isolated, plus capture the game cannot forge. Reserved until the capture spike (#246) shows a way; the check refuses this grade.

rows.mode: Replay sandbox: the game runs with no network, its own process tree and only its work copy, one output folder and its inputs
rows.profile: Linux with a bubblewrap that has --disable-userns and --size (the harness tries the real command and finds out), Godot only; elsewhere the replay runs without it and replay.json says why

evidence.shows: CI on main (0356aef), job seeded-bugs, bubblewrap 0.9.0: the 34 sandbox tests with none skipped, every seeded-bug replay with the sandbox required, and three verifications through the gate and the orchestrator's worker with the sandbox required (accept, reject, accept)

inside, a program and the real game each fail to open a socket, write outside, read a check or the verifier, and read the starting process's environment, while the same attempts succeed outside; a link left as the trace is refused; the clean game's frame and trace hashes are the same with and without

rows.limits: Godot only: the Unity player and the web replay are not sandboxed. The gate records how many replays were sandboxed and can require it, and the orchestrator's isolated class requires it; no verdict is graded isolated by it, because that grade also needs a trusted job that judges and signs (#254, #255). Not shown in the real tool: that the terminal was reachable before the sandbox got a session of its own. A namespace sandbox on the host's kernel, not a virtual machine. Total disk use of the work copy and the output folder is not limited, only each file; CPU and memory are limited only by the replay's time limit. On Ubuntu 24.04 the runner must allow unprivileged user namespaces first.

rows.mode: Verification as a job: verify, status, cancel and report, with a folder and a status file per job
rows.profile: The Godot game, through the CI gate's verification
rows.observer: The engine's record; no vision model

evidence.shows: CI on main (0356aef), job seeded-bugs: the sample command ran three real Godot verifications as jobs, each in a worker of its own with the replay sandbox required: accept for the game as it is, reject for the seeded bug, accept for the repair

two jobs keep to their own folders; a cancelled job stays cancelled and what it started is stopped; a killed worker leaves a failed job; a job out of time is needs-review; a missing tool is a diagnostic and needs-review; the Godot engine decides as the gate does, on a stand-in replay

one walk of a game folder makes every digest and every copy: the copy holds exactly the files the digest covers; the bundled games keep their digests; a link that leaves the checkout, a loop or a pipe stops a replay before anything is copied; a replay of another tree than the record names is not used

rows.limits: Only the sample command and tests call it: the gate's action and the site do not go through it yet. The isolated execution class runs every replay with the sandbox required and refuses where the machine cannot; its evidence grade stays diagnostic, because the ledger's isolated grade also needs a trusted job that judges and signs (#254, #255). The game is held to the tree the job asked about (the worker's read, the gate's record and each replay's copy must agree, or the job is needs-review), and the verifier judges with the one reading of the specs and routes whose digest is the job's. On a system without /proc a killed worker's children are not found and run on to their own time limit. One host.

nothing is accepted without recorded vision answers; a frame not in the recording is no answer and needs review; the publish check refuses anything outside its allowlist; the verify job holds no secret and the publish job runs no sample code
the home page and the README link the Run it page, and the page and its script are there

rows.limits: Visitors cannot start a run yet: the service that starts runs (apps/run-it-edge) is written and tested against a local stub but not deployed, so the page says it cannot start runs.
